title: Meditating on Scripture
definition: Meditating on Scripture is the prayerful dwelling of the mind and heart upon God's Word so that its truth is understood, treasured, remembered, and obeyed.
summary: Biblical meditation fills the heart with God's truth and turns that truth over in prayer, worship, trust, and obedience.
christFocus: The written Word bears witness to Christ, and meditation helps believers treasure Him, depend on His grace, and walk in His ways.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Meditating on Scripture is not emptying the mind or drifting into vague spirituality. It is the intentional, prayerful reflection on what God has said.

Meditation helps Scripture move from the page into the life. It gives time for truth to confront fear, correct false thinking, awaken worship, strengthen obedience, and deepen trust in the Lord.

The blessed person in Psalm 1 delights in the law of the Lord and meditates on it day and night. This kind of meditation forms stability, fruitfulness, and perseverance because the life is rooted in God's Word.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people read Scripture quickly but never let it settle into the heart. Meditating on Scripture matters because truth must be remembered, treasured, and practiced.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Choose a verse or passage and slowly reflect on it throughout the day. Ask what it reveals about God, Christ, sin, grace, obedience, and hope. Turn the passage into prayer.
